Before making decisions involving investing, legal, tax or accounting concerns, you should consult appropriate professionals regarding your speciﬁc situation. ‍

title: Fueling the AI SRE: How monday.com Standardized Observability for 600+ Services
summary: Tired of 3 AM pages and missing runbooks? Learn how monday.com built Observability Guard to automate alerts and log management for over 600 services.
body_text: You spent the last two months developing a new service, got all the approvals on your architecture design, and you’re ready to deploy to production. There’s one last checkbox you need to fill: Observability . It’s a small service, more of a helper, nothing critical. You spend a day setting CPU and memory alerts, and maybe an error-rate alert for the one endpoint you have. Thresholds? Whatever felt right at the moment. Runbook? I know my service; everybody knows how to deal with a CPU throttling alert. I’ll add more monitors as it scales up. Two years later, the service has served half of the production traffic, six other services depend on it, and you’ve never looked back at the alerting setup. In fact, you don’t even work there. You just started your first on-call rotation at your new company. And the very first night, you get the proverbial 3 AM page. You stare at a high-severity alert for an unfamiliar, business-critical service. You click the link. The dashboard is broken. You check for a runbook. There isn’t one. You search Slack, only to find a thread from two years ago written by an engineer who left the company last month, saying: “I know my service; everybody knows how to deal with a CPU throttling alert.” We’ve all been there, cursing our predecessors. Scaling the Nightmare to 600+ services At a small startup, this is a minor annoyance. At monday.com’s scale, managing this operational noise becomes critical to maintaining a seamless experience for millions of users. Our engineering culture focuses on giving engineers the freedom to choose the tools they use and how they use them to build the best Work OS platform. The observability tooling is no exception. We structure our observability tooling around OpenTelemetry instrumentation, giving us the liberty to choose from a range of observability and monitoring platforms. As a result of this freedom, our Observability team currently supports 10 different tools and vendors. When you let hundreds of developers manually configure their own observability across ten different tools, a few critical things break down at scale: The Wall of Noise : When thresholds are set based on “whatever feels right at the moment,” you get chaos. One team alerts at 70% CPU; another alerts at 95%. On-call engineers can easily face alert fatigue, making it harder to quickly isolate and prioritize critical signals. The Tribal Knowledge Abyss : Runbooks become a myth. They are scattered across obsolete documentation sites, Slack messages, or, worst of all, locked entirely inside the brains of engineers who have long since switched teams or left the company. Why Good Observability is Hard This friction doesn’t exist because the engineers are lazy (well, we are, but that’s what makes us well-suited for the job), but because observability is objectively hard to do right. It requires experience, deep infrastructure knowledge, and most importantly, time. When a team is pushing to ship a new feature, you can’t expect them to pause for a week to architect a flawless, future-proof alerting system from scratch. But you still need it to be done right. To break the cycle, we realized we couldn’t just tell engineers to “do better”. We needed a common, extensible framework that allows everyone to quickly set up standardized alerting for any service, new and old. Because when you strip away the business logic, the services are not actually that different from one another: The Baseline: Every single one of them needs a similar baseline of alerts on low-level signals. Everyone wants to know whether they’re approaching CPU or memory limits or whether their containers are stuck in a restart loop. The Dependencies: Depending on the other resources they use, such as queues, databases, and caches, the services need another set of alerts with a common structure, even if the specific thresholds differ. The Custom Logic: Only after those layers are solid should the service owners start thinking about custom alerts for their services’ specific use cases. The engineers shouldn’t be bothered with discovering the intricacies of our infrastructure to create a basic CPU alert and recreating the same runbook as every other team. Food for AI SRE Agents Beyond helping our human engineers, standardized alerts are crucial for the era of AI SRE Agents. Standardized alerts serve as a predictable data contract, providing AI agents with the precise context they need to operate. Zero Noise Correlation : Instead of forcing an AI to correlate between hundreds of subtly different, messy custom alerts that ultimately achieve the same goal, it gets a clean, unified signal. Tribal Knowledge Turned Institutional : Because the alert structure is uniform, the AI can instantly recall past incidents triggered by the exact same alert, matching the current issue with the specific “chain of thought” used to resolve it in the past. So, instead of asking every team to reinvent observability, we decided to build a single platform to meet all observability needs. And what better place to house it than Sphera, our Internal Developer Portal? (If you’re curious about how Sphera came to be, you can read about our journey to create an IDP here ). Meet the Observability Guard What we proudly call the Observability Guard is, in fact, yet another tab on the service page in Sphera. Its goal is to provide a single point of entry for all of the team’s observability needs. What started modestly as a templating engine today handles service metadata in our providers, manages storage tiers for our logs, proposes infrastructure changes, and enforces mandatory alerts. Let’s start with the basics: alerts . Alert Templates Everyone has some basic idea of what monitors every service needs. That knowledge grows with engineering experience, and we want to share it with everyone at monday.com. So we started with what our team knew best about alerting best practices, focusing on the Kubernetes infrastructure : pod and ArgoCD app status, resource usage, HPA approaching limits, and CronJob issues. To me, the default alerts provided by the kube-prometheus-stack always served as a good starting point. But our knowledge is limited, so we wanted to invite other teams to support this initiative. We needed a way to allow easy collaboration, so we decided to store the alert definitions as JSON templates in the Observability Guard git repository. Everyone at monday.com has access to this repo and can contribute. The biggest contributors, naturally, are the teams closest to the production infrastructure: Production Engineering and Database Reliability Engineering . The product development teams, being on the receiving end of the alerts, mostly contribute to the quality of the alerts by enhancing runbooks, managing grouping, and configuring filters. By fostering a sense of common ownership, we built an impressive catalog of 107 alert templates . Resource Discovery One generic alert for all your pods might be enough, but your endpoints or queues will certainly need more flexibility. We started simple: a single blanket alert for all SQS queues. The flaw? A one-size-fits-all threshold only protects your largest queue. If a smaller queue backed up, it would never cross that high threshold, leaving localized anomalies undetected by the blanket rule. To solve this, we used our internal cloud inventory service to build automated resource discovery. Here is how the functionality works now: The Blanket Default: We keep things simple with a broad wildcard alert. It catches all your queues under a single, standard baseline rule. Smart Overrides: If an engineer needs a custom threshold for a specific queue, they can set it. The system automatically applies the new rule and excludes that specific queue from the blanket alert so they don’t get double-alerted. Stop the Guesswork How do you determine the correct alerting threshold? You have to find a precise point, balancing between being woken up at night and missing the incident. It’s an art form in itself. Observability Guard analyzes the metric’s past behavior and automatically proposes a fitting threshold. Our go-to method is Median Absolute Deviation (MAD). Why MAD? Traditional standard deviation is easily skewed by wild, temporary anomalies; a single massive spike can ruin your baseline. MAD is more robust against outliers because it focuses on the median, giving a much truer reflection of normal behavior. The algorithm calculates thresholds in three steps: Find the Baseline : It calculates the median metric value over a set timeframe (default: 14 days). Calculate the Variance : It measures how far each data point deviates from that baseline and finds the median of those deviations. Set the Alert Thresholds : It establishes thresholds using a basic multiplier: k*MAD, where k=3 for warnings and k=5 for critical alerts. Of course, no algorithm knows your code better than your engineers. We strongly encourage teams to override the defaults and set custom thresholds whenever they have specific domain knowledge. To aid them in crafting those custom thresholds, the tool exposes the MAD calculation in a clean graphical interface, alongside other key historical data points like max, median, and percentiles. All in a graphical interface. It’s also available as an AI skill for those who don’t believe in clicking on the Web anymore. Log Management While managing alerts saved our engineers time, we realized the Guard could also tackle another massive data headache: dynamic log management. Every person who has to manage logging platforms knows this pain. Your log quota is running out, and you have to find someone to sacrifice their logs for the greater good. You found somebody? Great, now they need to change the log level or tags in the code and deploy it, or, if you’re using a log gateway, make that change there. This is exactly the kind of manual, low-level infrastructure friction Observability Guard was built to remove. Instead of forcing teams to manually refactor code just to manage data volume, we built log management directly into Guard’s capabilities. Our logging system uses tiers for storing logs, allowing teams to drastically optimize storage costs for high-volume, non-critical debug logs that don’t require active alerting or real-time dashboards. By default, only info and lower log levels are sent to the lowest tier. Errors and warnings will end up in the alerting-capable tiers. However, not all errors are equal. Some subsystems of your service are mission-critical, while issues in others can be just logged for debugging. Observability Guard gives developers this flexibility. Every subsystem can be managed differently, on the fly. The change is propagated instantly to the provider’s systems. It’s the exact same vision we brought to alerting: shifting complex operational decisions away from manual code changes and onto a unified, automated control plane. Adoption Promoting new features at monday.com is easy; we regularly share the advancements on Slack channels with all Builders. We have bi-weekly summaries of small improvements from all the Infra teams. And there are Learning & Development sessions where you can do a live demo and win people over. It doesn’t mean everyone switched overnight; it was still a long, gradual process. But every time someone approached us for help with the alerting setup, we promoted the Observability Guard. If it couldn’t do what they needed, we added that feature. We prioritized the development, at the cost of other tasks in the backlog, because we were confident it would save us time in the long run. But what’s most important is that Observability Guard genuinely makes engineers’ lives easier, and they want to use it; they want it to improve. No one misses clicking through three different platforms to set up alerts or finding out that the monitor doesn’t work because of wrong assumptions about data aggregation. Centralized platforms shouldn’t add toil or be yet another place to visit on the service’s onboarding journey. They should shift focus from external, specialized platforms to a single pane of glass that lets engineers do most of the work. They’ll still need to visit them for in-depth investigations, but they should always start in a familiar place that’s always up to date. Groundwork for Mandatory Alerts For over a year, the Observability Guard was an opt-in feature. Over this time, it has become the standard way of creating alerts. This year, we moved even further, introducing mandatory alerts for the signals we are the most confident in. Observability Guard provides a strong foundation for such an initiative. It alleviated the technical issues, allowing the focus to be solely on the social perspective. It’s hard to convince teams to let external forces into their carefully crafted alerting schemes. But to take our system reliability to the next level, we had to develop a process to enable confident adoption. How did we do that while minimizing disruption to our colleagues’ sleep and keeping the number of false positives low? That’s a story for another blog post. What It Gave Us We started this journey looking at the cycle every software engineer has lived through: the 3 AM page, broken dashboard, missing runbook, and the ghost of a predecessor who left the company months ago. At a scale of 600+ services and 10 different vendors, solving this wasn’t about nagging developers to write better documentation or manually build their alerts. It required a complete redefinition of where and how observability happens. By building Observability Guard directly into Sphera, we turned observability from the least favorite chore into an automated, out-of-the-box standard. The New Normal at monday.com Shifting the alerting control plane to our Internal Developer Portal has rewritten the rules of how we scale observability: For our Human Engineers: It provides a single pane of glass that eliminates platform-hopping, automatically calculates smart thresholds, and ensures that an accurate, crowdsourced runbook is always attached to an alert. For our AI SRE Agents: It establishes a clean, predictable data contract, allowing LLMs to accurately correlate signals without tripping over a messy web of custom alert configurations. For our Infrastructure: It guarantees robust visibility across hundreds of services without sacrificing the tool autonomy that fuels our engineering culture. Turning Tribal into Institutional Centralized platforms shouldn’t just be another tool in the shed; they should optimize the entire process by institutionalizing the tribal knowledge of your best engineers. Observability shouldn’t require you to be a digital archaeologist every time a service acts up. By abstracting away the low-level noise, automating the baselines, and building a culture of shared infrastructure ownership, we gave our engineers their peace of mind back. This kind of cultural shift doesn’t happen overnight. You have to start small and win people over with obvious, immediate quality-of-life improvements. But when you make doing the right thing the easiest path available, you don’t just build a more resilient system. You ensure everyone finally gets a good night’s sleep.

title: Business English With AI: Meetings, Negotiations, Roleplay (August 2026)
summary: Master business English for meetings and negotiations in August 2026 with AI roleplay, phrase banks, and on-demand spoken practice scenarios.
body_text: Picture the last time you had to disagree with someone in a meeting, in English, with real consequences. Did the words come out the way they did in your head? For most non-native speakers, there's a frustrating gap between what you can write and what you can say under pressure. AI roleplay won't close that gap overnight, but it gives you a way to practice English for business meetings on your own schedule, as many times as you need. TLDR: Most professional English contexts sit between B1 and C1; if you can read a proposal but freeze when asked your view, roleplay practice closes that gap faster than grammar drills. Learn five functional phrase banks before industry vocabulary: hedging, pushing back, buying time, interrupting, and confirming understanding are what hold a meeting together. A 2024 systematic review of 24 studies on AI chatbots for speaking practice found gains in confidence, engagement, and anxiety reduction, which maps directly to what business English demands. Courses build knowledge of forms; AI roleplay builds the retrieval side, closing the gap Swain's Output Hypothesis identifies between knowing a phrase and producing it under real-time pressure. ISSEN runs custom spoken business scenarios with real-time conversational feedback on vocabulary and phrasing, cross-session memory, and conversation-anchored flashcards at under $1 per session at daily use. Can AI help you practice business English? Yes. AI voice tutors can simulate the meetings, negotiations, and cold intros you rehearse before doing them for real, at any hour, without a scheduled partner. They handle spoken drills for common professional scenarios well. What they cannot replace is reading the room, coaching body language, or juggling three native-speed accents talking over each other. Treat AI practice as the volume layer under a broader plan that includes real colleagues, recorded meetings, and, when possible, a human coach for cultural feedback. A 2024 systematic review of 24 studies on AI speaking practice reported gains in confidence, engagement, and anxiety reduction, which is exactly the training ground professional English contexts demand. What CEFR level does business English require? Business English is less about a single fluency threshold and more about matching your level to the room you are in. Most professional contexts sit between B1 and C1, and the tasks inside each band are specific. At B1 (IELTS 4.5 to 5.0), you can follow routine meetings, give direct instructions, and handle predictable client emails. At B2 (IELTS 5.5 to 6.5), you can lead a discussion, present quarterly results, and run a client call without a script. At C1 (IELTS 7.0 to 8.0), you can chair a high-stakes meeting, negotiate a contract, and shift register on the fly. If you can read a proposal but freeze when your manager asks for your view, you are likely B1 reaching for B2. That plateau is where AI English fluency practice pays off fastest. What business English vocabulary should you learn first? Grammar drills teach you to build sentences. Meetings ask you to steer them. The vocabulary that separates a B2 professional from a stalled one is functional: short phrases that buy time, soften disagreement, and confirm meaning without breaking flow. AI English learning for non-native speakers covers which of these patterns transfer fastest. Learn these five function banks first. Rehearse them out loud before you touch industry jargon. Hedging "I'd want to check that before we commit." "In principle, yes. The details we'd need to look at." "I'm inclined to agree, subject to timelines." Pushing back politely "I take that point, though my concern is the runway." "That's fair. Can I offer another angle?" "I see it slightly differently, if I can explain." Buying time "Let me make sure I understand what you're asking." "Give me a second to think that through." "Can I park that and circle back?" Interrupting "If I could jump in for a second." "Sorry to cut across, but there's something worth flagging." "Just to build on what Sara said." Confirming understanding "So what we're agreeing is that marketing owns Q2 delivery." "Just to play that back: two milestones, one owner, end of month." "So the ask is X by Friday. Have I got that right?" The words for your field will come from the work itself. The scaffolding above is what holds a conversation together while you find them. The business English scenario library Below is a drop-in library. Pick a row, copy the prompt into any AI English speaking app , and speak. Paste it, then start the call. Scenario CEFR Target phrases Roleplay prompt Performance review B2 "I'd frame that as," "one area I want to grow" You are my manager running my mid-year review. Ask about wins, gaps, and goals. Push back if answers are vague. Native pace. Salary negotiation B2 to C1 "based on market data," "a range closer to," "could we look at" You are HR. I'm asking for a 15 percent raise. Offer 6. Negotiate realistically. Stay in role. Standup update B1 "yesterday I shipped," "today I'm blocked on" You are my tech lead. Ask for yesterday, today, blockers. Interrupt if I ramble past 45 seconds. Client escalation B2 "I understand this isn't the outcome you expected," "what would resolve this" You are an angry enterprise client. Our product broke a workflow. Vent for 30 seconds, then let me lead the recovery. Disagreeing with a senior colleague C1 "my hesitation is," "can we pressure-test that assumption" You are a VP two levels above me. Defend a strategy I think is wrong. Let me disagree without backing down. Closing a deal B2 to C1 "what would need to be true for you to sign this week" You are a mid-market buyer at the end of a sales cycle. Procurement is stalling. Push me to earn the close. Run one scenario per session. Ten minutes is enough to expose the phrases you reach for under pressure, which suits the AI language apps for busy adults who cannot block out larger windows. How do you roleplay a job interview with an AI tutor? Set the scene in one line, then hand the tutor the constraints. Something like: "You are a hiring manager at a Series B fintech interviewing me for a senior PM role. Respond at C1 level, use technical vocabulary, and interrupt me if my answer runs over 90 seconds. Ask two competency questions, then throw one unexpected follow-up." The unpredictability is the point. Scripted prep tools let you rehearse polished answers to expected questions; the best AI language tutors for conversation force you to produce language you have not pre-loaded. That pressure surfaces the gap Merrill Swain's Output Hypothesis names: knowing a phrase and retrieving it under stress are separate skills. After each run, isolate one weak point (rambling, filler words, freezing on "tell me about a time") and rerun the same prompt with a tighter constraint on that behavior. How do you practice negotiating in English? Negotiation English moves faster than meeting English and hides more. Speakers anchor with numbers, concede without conceding, reframe an offer as a question, and close by letting silence do the work. Speed, ambiguity, and face-saving indirection trip non-native speakers up, not vocabulary. Set up the drill like this. Tell your tutor: "You are a procurement manager at a mid-market SaaS buyer. I am selling. Push back hard on price at B2 to C1 level. Use hedging and conditionals. Run three exchanges. Do not concede easily." Focus each exchange on one move type below. Anchoring "Where we typically land for a team of your size is around X." "Before we get to numbers, what does success look like on your side?" Conceding "I could see a path to that, provided we lock a two-year term." "I'd need to check, but in principle, yes." Reframing "Instead of a discount, could we look at extended payment terms?" "If price is the blocker, what would the right number unlock?" Closing "So if I can get you to X, we're signing this quarter?" "What would need to be true for procurement to move today?" Run the same three exchanges twice. The second pass is where conditional grammar starts landing without conscious effort. Is AI roleplay better than a business English course? A well-run business English course gives you frameworks: report structures, email registers, presentation openings, the grammar of formal writing. It also gives you a syllabus, which matters when you have a BEC exam or a certificate deadline. What it rarely offers is enough unscripted speaking time for retrieval to become automatic. AI roleplay adds what courses skip: retrieval under real-time pressure, converting known forms into automatic speech. The AI vs. human tutor tradeoff maps onto Swain's distinction between knowing a form and producing it under real-time pressure, a gap most classroom hours cannot close because 12 learners cannot each get 40 minutes of open-ended speaking per session. Use the course for structure. Use AI roleplay for volume. The combination beats either alone. How AI tutors for business English compare in 2026 ISSEN offers custom scenarios, unscripted roleplay, and real-time in-conversation correction at under $1 per session at daily use, with no scheduling required. Langua (LanguaTalk) also supports custom scenarios and unscripted roleplay, with post-turn feedback at roughly $1 to $2 per session and no scheduling required. ELSA Speak is pronunciation-first, limited to scripted drills and pronunciation feedback, at $0.50 to $1 per session with no scheduling required. Preply and italki are human-tutor marketplaces: both offer live custom scenarios and real-time correction, but sessions run $20 to $50 each and require advance scheduling. Babbel Live uses pre-set business tracks in a guided group format with teacher-led feedback at $10 to $15 per group session, on fixed slots. Preply and italki are human-tutor marketplaces. Three $30 sessions a week runs $360 a month, and a coach will catch cultural missteps an AI misses. Professionals working in multilingual markets (for example, those studying French for business and work ) often find the hybrid model most effective. An AI voice tutor at $20 to $29 a month gives unlimited reps, which fits daily practice better. Use the human tutor for accountability and cultural correction. Use the AI for the hours in between. Competitor pricing and features verified August 2026; check each provider's live site before subscribing. Tiers move. ISSEN: practice business English with an AI voice tutor Every scenario above runs inside ISSEN as a full spoken conversation. Paste the roleplay prompt, hit start, and you are in a live business meeting in under 30 seconds. Custom scenarios let you script the exact setup line by line: role, register, pushback level, interruption rules. Three features matter for professional practice. Smart turn detection means no push-to-talk, so the tutor interrupts and lets itself be interrupted the way a real colleague would. AI language tutoring for speaking fluency relies heavily on this kind of adaptation: cross-session memory keeps track of the structures you fumbled last week and works them back into this week's roleplay. Conversation-anchored flashcards surface the words you actually used, tied to the sentence you used them in. ISSEN runs on iOS, Android, and web for $20 to $29 USD per month (verify current pricing on issen.com), well below a single italki or Preply session. Try ISSEN free for 10 minutes. Final thoughts on practicing English for real business conversations Your reading and writing may be at B2, but the moment your manager asks for your view in a live call, that is where the gap shows up. Targeted roleplay on the specific scenarios you face at work is what closes it, and ten focused minutes a day builds the retrieval speed that courses alone cannot. Try ISSEN free for 10 minutes and run one of these scenarios before your next meeting. FAQs What's the difference between using ISSEN and Preply or italki to practice English for business meetings? ISSEN gives you unlimited on-demand speaking reps at under $1 per session at daily use, while Preply and italki sessions run $20 to $50 each and require scheduling in advance. The practical split is this: use a human tutor on Preply or italki for periodic cultural correction and structured accountability, and use ISSEN for the daily volume that weekly sessions cannot supply. Can I practice specific business English scenarios like salary negotiations or client escalations with an AI tutor? Yes. You can paste a custom roleplay prompt directly into ISSEN, specifying the role, register, pushback level, and interruption rules, and be in a live spoken conversation within 30 seconds. The scenario library in the blog includes ready-to-use prompts for negotiations, performance reviews, standups, and deal-closing at B1 through C1 level. Is AI roleplay a replacement for a business English course? The two cover different gaps, so neither replaces the other. A course builds declarative knowledge: report structures, email registers, formal grammar. AI roleplay builds retrieval under pressure, which is the gap Swain's Output Hypothesis identifies as what classroom hours rarely close when 12 learners share one session. Use the course for structure and AI roleplay for the speaking volume that converts knowledge into automatic speech. What CEFR level do you need to lead a business meeting in English? Leading a meeting comfortably sits at B2, where you can present results and run a client call without a script. Chairing high-stakes meetings or negotiating contracts requires C1, where register-shifting mid-conversation becomes reliable. If you can follow a meeting but freeze when asked for your view, you are likely at B1 reaching for B2, which is the exact plateau where structured roleplay practice produces the fastest gains. How do you set up a job interview roleplay with an AI voice tutor that actually prepares you for unpredictable questions? Give the tutor a one-line scene with explicit constraints: role, seniority level, language difficulty, time limits, and an instruction to add an unexpected follow-up question. The unpredictability matters because scripted prep tools let you rehearse polished answers to expected questions, while open-ended AI response forces you to produce language you have not pre-loaded, and that is precisely the pressure that surfaces gaps in real-time retrieval.

title: The barbell season: why your Q4 plan needs two peaks, not one
summary: Retailers are still building holiday media plans around a single curve: slow build in October, ramp through November, peak at Black Friday and Cyber Monday, tail off in December. That curve doesn't exist anymore.
body_text: Retailers are still building holiday media plans around a single curve: slow build in October, ramp through November, peak at Black Friday and Cyber Monday, tail off in December. That curve doesn’t exist anymore. Holiday shopping in 2025 split into two distinct peaks with a soft middle between them. Nearly a quarter of holiday budgets, 24% , were already spent before November 1, the highest share in five years. At the same time, 60% of shoppers didn’t expect to finish their holiday shopping until December. Consideration isn’t a Black Friday problem. It’s an October problem for one group of shoppers and a December problem for another, and a single undifferentiated November plan misses both. Why this happened Wish lists are being built earlier. Consumers are narrowing consideration sets for larger purchases well ahead of peak shopping windows, with many of those decisions locked in by October. Brands that show up only in November are showing up after a meaningful share of shoppers has already decided. At the same time, a growing share of shoppers are deliberately waiting. NRF projected 158.9 million consumers would shop on the last Saturday before Christmas alone, evidence that the late window isn’t shrinking, it’s intensifying. What this means for budget allocation A plan that spends evenly across October through December is optimizing for an audience that doesn’t exist. The early-window shopper and the late-window shopper are different people with different intent signals, and they need to be reached with different timing, different messaging, and in many cases different channels entirely. The practical shift: front-load consideration-stage investment into September and October, when value-driven shoppers are locking in decisions, and maintain a strong last-mile presence through December for the shoppers who haven’t finished yet. The middle of November, the period most Q4 plans over-invest in by habit, is actually the least differentiated moment in the entire season. The cost of waiting There’s a pricing penalty to treating Q4 as a single peak, too. Waiting until the traditional “peak” window to activate means competing for inventory after prices have already climbed, a dynamic worth its own conversation in our next post on Q4 CPM pressure. This isn’t just a consumer behavior shift, either. It’s showing up in how advertisers themselves are buying. According to Perion’s own Q4 2026 Holiday Tentpole analysis, roughly a third of Q4 insertion orders now close in July through September, the real advance-booking window, rather than in the traditional October-to-November rush. Part of that is simple math: with an average 54-day sales cycle from RFP to close, per that same analysis, a campaign that needs to be live in October has to have its paperwork in by mid-August, or it’s chasing inventory that’s already been claimed. That same analysis found retail alone sees close to 60% of its Q4 media business wrap up in this July-through-November window. The advertisers moving fastest aren’t reacting to a forecast, they’re reacting to the same reality this piece opened with: the consideration window starts earlier than the campaign calendar assumes, and the budget is following it there. For now, the operating principle is simple: stop planning for a bell curve. Plan for a barbell, one budget strategy for the early consideration window, another for the late surge, and build in the flexibility to shift between them as the season actually unfolds rather than as originally forecast. Planning for two peaks instead of one is the first shift. The next is knowing how to manage the budget once the campaign is live, shifting spend daily, adjusting creative in flight, reacting to inventory and demand signals as they change. If you want to talk through how your Q4 plan handles that, contact us today . Found this useful? Share it: Perion Marketing

title: BILL Reports Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results

title: Deutsche Bank supports Quinbrook’s Supernode Stage 3 Battery Energy Storage System
summary: Deutsche Bank supports Quinbrook’s Supernode Stage 3 Battery Energy Storage System
body_text: Deutsche Bank has committed 85 million Australian dollars as an Original Lender in the financing of Quinbrook’s Supernode Stage 3 Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) in Queensland, Australia, further supporting the development of one of the country's largest battery storage precincts. Deutsche Bank's commitment forms part of the project's 469 million Australian dollar senior secured, non-recourse financing package, supporting the construction and operation of the asset. The project will play an important role in strengthening grid stability and supporting Queensland's transition away from emissions-intensive sources of power. We are delighted to continue our partnership with Quinbrook through the financing of Supernode 3, marking our second transaction together and further strengthening our collaboration across the Supernode platform. title: AI Vendor Communication in Property Management: 2026 Guide
body_text: TL;DR AI vendor communication is the use of artificial intelligence to automate the back-and-forth between property managers and maintenance vendors, covering everything from dispatch notifications to scheduling, status updates, follow-ups, and escalation. It replaces the phone tag, missed emails, and forgotten check-ins that slow down work orders and damage vendor relationships. Properties using AI dispatch report 25 to 35 percent faster resolution times compared to manual assignment, and the automation can save a 500-unit operation nearly $36,000 per year in labor costs alone. Vendor coordination is the unglamorous backbone of property management maintenance. When a toilet overflows at 2 AM or an HVAC unit dies during a heat wave, the speed and quality of communication between your team and the vendor determines whether the issue gets resolved in hours or drags on for days. Most property managers know the pain: calling a plumber, leaving a voicemail, waiting, calling again, texting the backup, forgetting to update the tenant, then scrambling to log everything in the PMS after the fact. AI vendor communication exists to eliminate that entire cycle. Explore Haven’s Maintenance AI to see how automated vendor coordination works in practice. Quick Answer: What Is AI Vendor Communication? AI vendor communication uses artificial intelligence to automate maintenance-related communication between property managers, vendors, and tenants. Instead of relying on phone calls, emails, and manual follow-ups, AI automatically: - Selects vendors - Sends dispatch notifications - Coordinates scheduling - Provides status updates - Escalates non-responses - Verifies job completion - Updates the property management system In practice, AI reduces maintenance coordination from approximately 30 minutes per work order to about 5 minutes while improving vendor response times and accelerating maintenance resolution. Key takeaway: AI doesn't replace vendors. It automates the communication layer that connects tenants, vendors, and property managers. AI Vendor Communication Definition Term Definition AI vendor communication AI-powered maintenance coordination between property managers and service vendors Primary goal Automate maintenance-related communication Core functions Dispatch, scheduling, status updates, follow-up, escalation Users Property managers, maintenance coordinators, vendors Common channels SMS, email, voice, PMS messaging Expected outcome Faster maintenance resolution What Is AI Vendor Communication? AI vendor communication refers to the use of artificial intelligence to manage the exchange of information between a property management operation and its service vendors. This includes dispatch notifications, scope-of-work delivery, scheduling confirmations, real-time status updates, follow-up messages, completion verification, and escalation when a vendor fails to respond. It sits within the broader AI maintenance coordinator workflow, connecting the moment a work order is created to the moment the job is done and the tenant is notified. The term is distinct from vendor management platforms (which focus on onboarding, compliance, and payment) and from outsourced vendor networks (which replace your preferred vendors with their own). AI vendor communication is about the messaging layer, making sure the right information reaches the right vendor at the right time, and that nobody falls through the cracks. Why AI Vendor Communication Matters The Manual Communication Problem Property management is, as one YC-backed startup founder put it, “human-intensive, low-margin, and full of repetitive communication.” Operators juggle leasing calls, maintenance triage, and support inquiries while managing staff turnover and fragmented tools. Vendor coordination is where these pressures converge. A single work order handled manually takes about 30 minutes of coordination time. Multiply that across dozens of active work orders and you’re looking at 2 to 3 hours of supervisor time consumed daily just by dispatch decisions, according to OxMaint’s operational research. Property management companies miss more than 60% of inbound calls in many cases, which means vendor callbacks and scheduling confirmations often go unanswered too. The Retention Connection Speed matters more than most operators realize. Companies with sub-1-hour dispatch times retain 12% more tenants annually than those with 4+ hour dispatch times, according to the RentCafe 2025 Operational Report . That gap is enormous when you calculate the cost of turnover, make-ready, and vacancy. Vendor Relationship Damage Poor communication doesn’t just frustrate tenants. It burns through vendor relationships. According to NARPM’s 2025 survey, the average property management company loses 4.3 vendor relationships per year due to payment delays, communication breakdowns, and scheduling conflicts. Losing a reliable plumber or electrician in a tight market can set operations back months. AI vendor communication directly addresses the communication breakdown piece by ensuring vendors receive complete information, timely follow-ups, and consistent professionalism. For more on how after-hours gaps amplify these problems, see this guide on after-hours maintenance AI . What AI Vendor Communication Actually Does: Step by Step Understanding AI vendor communication means understanding the specific touchpoints it handles. Here’s the sequence. 1. Dispatch Notification with Full Context When a work order is created (either by the tenant, an AI intake system, or the property manager), the AI selects the appropriate vendor and sends a structured assignment. This isn’t a bare-bones email saying “plumbing issue, unit 4B.” AI systems analyze vendor performance history, current availability, geographic proximity, trade specialization, and cost considerations to pick the right match. The dispatch message includes the full picture: issue description, photos or video from the tenant, unit access instructions, tenant contact info, and any relevant history. This matters more than people think. Practitioners on forums have noted that some vendor networks send assignments with so little context that vendors reject jobs or show up unprepared, leading to incomplete repairs and wasted trips. For a deeper look at the routing logic, read about AI vendor routing . 2. Scheduling Coordination Once the vendor accepts, the AI coordinates timing. It can cross-reference the vendor’s availability with the tenant’s preferred windows and confirm an appointment without the property manager touching anything. This eliminates the three-way phone tag that typically consumes a chunk of every maintenance coordinator’s morning. 3. Bidirectional Status Updates This is where AI vendor communication separates itself from basic automation. The AI sends progress notifications in both directions: vendors receive reminders and check-ins, while tenants receive updates on when their issue will be addressed. Property managers stay in the loop with everything the AI is doing, without having to ask. One key advantage: AI can speak to many people at the same time. As the founder of Brickwise (a YC-backed maintenance platform) explained, as soon as the AI picks up an issue, it can contact dozens of contractors simultaneously. Manual coordination is sequential. You call one vendor, wait, call the next. AI runs parallel outreach instantly. 4. Follow-Up and Completion Verification The real value of AI vendor communication isn’t the initial dispatch. It’s the persistent follow-up. AI doesn’t forget to check whether the vendor showed up. It doesn’t lose track of open work orders during a busy week. It confirms job completion, collects feedback, and closes the work order in the PMS automatically. For more on what happens after the vendor finishes, check out this guide on AI maintenance follow-up . 5. Escalation When a vendor doesn’t respond within the expected timeframe, AI automatically escalates. It can ping backup vendors, alert the property manager, or both. This is governed by configurable AI escalation rules that match the urgency of the situation. How AI Vendor Communication Fits Into the Maintenance Workflow Vendor communication is only one component of the AI maintenance lifecycle. A complete AI maintenance workflow typically includes: Tenant maintenance intake Emergency triage Work order creation Vendor selection Vendor communication Repair tracking Completion verification Tenant feedback collection PMS documentation Analytics and reporting Property managers evaluating AI tools should avoid looking at vendor communication in isolation. The greatest efficiency gains occur when communication, dispatch, triage, and documentation are integrated into a single workflow. AI Vendor Communication Workflow at a Glance Stage AI Action Human Involvement Work order creation Receives maintenance request Optional Vendor selection Chooses the best vendor Approval if required Dispatch Sends assignment None Scheduling Coordinates availability Optional Status updates Monitors job progress None Follow-up Requests completion confirmation None Escalation Contacts backup vendors Manager notification PMS documentation Logs all interactions None Communication Channels AI Uses AI vendor communication isn’t locked to a single channel. Effective systems use a combination of: SMS is the workhorse. Most vendors check texts before email, especially field technicians who are on job sites. SMS is ideal for dispatch notifications, scheduling confirmations, and quick status requests. Email works well for detailed scope-of-work delivery, including photos, documents, and longer instructions that vendors may need to reference later. Voice matters for urgent situations and for vendors who prefer phone calls. A voice-first AI system can call vendors directly, explain the issue, and confirm acceptance in real time. PMS portal messages keep everything documented within the property management system, creating a paper trail that’s useful for audits, disputes, and owner reporting. Why does multichannel matter? Because vendors have preferences. A 25-year-old handyman might respond to texts in seconds but ignore emails for days. A veteran HVAC company might want a phone call for anything over a certain dollar amount. The best AI vendor communication systems adapt to these preferences rather than forcing a single channel. For more on the tenant-facing side of multichannel communication, see this piece on 24/7 tenant communication tools . Best Use Cases for AI Vendor Communication Multifamily Communities High work order volume makes maintenance coordination difficult. AI reduces dispatcher workload while improving tenant communication. Single-Family Rental Portfolios Small teams managing large geographic areas benefit from automated scheduling and vendor outreach. Student Housing Student turnover creates frequent maintenance requests. AI ensures consistent vendor communication during peak periods. HOA and Community Associations AI provides centralized communication across multiple vendors while maintaining complete documentation. Build-to-Rent Communities Standardized maintenance procedures make these portfolios ideal candidates for automation. AI Vendor Communication vs. Manual Vendor Coordination Here’s what the same work order looks like under both approaches. Step Manual Process AI Vendor Communication Vendor selection PM mentally recalls who’s available, checks spreadsheet or contacts list AI evaluates performance history, proximity, availability, and cost in seconds Dispatch PM calls or texts vendor, may need to try 2-3 before getting a response AI contacts multiple vendors simultaneously with full context Context delivery PM verbally describes issue, may forget details or photos AI compiles tenant report, photos, access info, and history into structured message Scheduling Three-way phone tag between PM, vendor, and tenant AI cross-references availability and confirms automatically Status updates Tenant calls PM asking for updates; PM calls vendor asking for updates AI proactively sends updates to all parties Follow-up PM may forget to check if vendor completed the job AI automatically verifies completion and closes work order Documentation PM logs notes in PMS after the fact (if they remember) AI logs every interaction in real time via PMS notes and logging Time per work order ~30 minutes ~5 minutes of oversight The documentation advantage deserves emphasis. With manual coordination, critical details live in text message threads, voicemails, and the property manager’s memory. When staff turns over, that institutional knowledge vanishes. AI vendor communication creates a complete, searchable record of every interaction. Organizations using AI in property management report a 20 to 30% improvement in operational efficiency and save up to 10 hours per week, according to industry surveys. AI Vendor Communication ROI Calculator The financial impact of AI becomes easier to understand when you calculate labor savings. Portfolio Size Work Orders Per Month Estimated Labor Savings 100 units 100 $7,200/year 250 units 250 $18,000/year 500 units 500 $36,000/year 1,000 units 1,000 $72,000/year Example calculation: Manual coordination: 30 minutes per work order AI-assisted coordination: 5 minutes per work order Time saved: 25 minutes Monthly work orders: 500 Hourly labor cost: $35 Annual savings: 500 × 25 minutes × $35/hour × 12 months = approximately $36,000 Common Confusion Points AI Vendor Communication ≠ Vendor Management Platforms Vendor management platforms like VendorPM focus on onboarding, insurance tracking, W-9 collection, and payment processing. They manage the vendor relationship lifecycle. AI vendor communication manages the day-to-day messaging for active work orders. The two are complementary, not interchangeable. AI Vendor Communication ≠ Outsourced Vendor Networks Services like Lula or Lessen provide their own vendor networks to handle maintenance. This is a fundamentally different model. One RentRedi user review captured the concern well: “I do not recommend the maintenance vendor Lessen due to some companies are not that good and honest. However, communication through the app for maintenance requests using your own people for tenant requests are ideal.” Property managers consistently prefer AI that works with their own vendor lists rather than replacing trusted relationships with unknown contractors. This preference makes sense. You’ve spent years building relationships with reliable local vendors. AI vendor communication should strengthen those relationships, not bypass them. AI Vendor Communication ≠ Automated Email Templates Setting up canned email responses in your PMS is not AI vendor communication. Templates are static. They don’t adapt to context, they can’t handle scheduling logistics, and they certainly don’t follow up when a vendor goes silent. True AI vendor communication involves dynamic, context-aware messaging that responds to changing conditions throughout the work order lifecycle. For a broader view of how these tools fit into the AI property management software category, that page breaks down the full suite of capabilities. What to Look For in an AI Vendor Communication System If you’re evaluating AI tools for vendor coordination, these are the capabilities that separate useful products from marketing fluff. PMS integration depth. The AI needs read and write access to your property management system. It should create work orders, assign vendors, update statuses, and log notes directly, not just send messages and hope someone enters the data manually. Check whether the system integrates with your specific PMS through the vendor’s integrations page. Preferred vendor list support. This is non-negotiable for most operators. The AI should pull from your existing vendor relationships, respecting trade categories, service areas, and any performance tiers you’ve established. AI that routes work to unknown third-party networks defeats the purpose. For implementation details, read about AI vendor list integration . Context-rich dispatch messages. Ask to see an example of what the vendor actually receives. Does it include photos? Tenant-reported details? Unit access instructions? Maintenance history? A well-structured AI dispatch message gives the vendor everything they need to show up prepared. Multichannel capability. SMS, email, and voice at minimum. The system should be able to reach vendors through whatever channel gets the fastest response. Follow-up automation. The initial dispatch is table stakes. What happens when the vendor doesn’t respond in 30 minutes? What about after the job is marked complete? Does the AI verify with the tenant? The follow-up loop is where most of the time savings actually come from. Emergency triage accuracy. Property Meld’s data estimates a 40% false emergency rate as the industry baseline, meaning four out of ten after-hours dispatches are for issues that aren’t actually emergencies. Good AI vendor communication starts with accurate triage so vendors aren’t dispatched unnecessarily. Haven’s Maintenance AI covers the full vendor communication loop, from intake and triage through work order creation inside the PMS, vendor dispatch from preferred vendor lists, and follow-up after completion. It operates across voice, SMS, and email channels. Book a demo with Haven to see AI vendor communication in action. Related Terms Vendor dispatch automation: The specific subset of AI vendor communication focused on selecting and notifying vendors when a new work order is created. Learn more in this vendor dispatch automation guide . Work order automation: The broader workflow of creating, assigning, tracking, and closing maintenance requests with AI assistance. Vendor communication is one component within this workflow. Emergency maintenance triage: The AI process of evaluating whether a maintenance request is a true emergency requiring immediate vendor dispatch or a routine issue that can wait for business hours. AI maintenance coordinator: The AI agent role that orchestrates the entire maintenance workflow, including tenant communication, vendor communication, PMS updates, and escalation. See the full AI maintenance coordinator guide for details. KPIs to Measure After Implementing AI Vendor Communication Property managers should track these metrics before and after implementation: KPI Manual Average AI-Assisted Target Dispatch time 30 minutes <5 minutes Vendor response time 1-2 hours <30 minutes Resolution time 24-72 hours 25-35% faster Open work orders Baseline Reduced Vendor retention Baseline Improved Tenant satisfaction Baseline Improved Without baseline measurements, it's difficult to quantify AI's impact. Frequently Asked Questions What types of messages does AI send to vendors? AI vendor communication handles dispatch notifications (with full job context), scheduling confirmation requests, status check-ins, follow-up reminders for non-responsive vendors, completion verification requests, and payment-related notifications. Each message is generated dynamically based on the specific work order, vendor, and situation rather than pulled from a static template. Does AI vendor communication replace my existing vendors? No. AI vendor communication works with your preferred vendor lists. It automates the messaging and coordination layer between you and your vendors. It does not replace them with third-party contractor networks. The goal is to make your existing vendor relationships more efficient, not to substitute unknown providers. How fast can AI dispatch a vendor compared to manual coordination? Research shows maintenance dispatch drops from approximately 30 minutes per work order to about 5 minutes with AI automation. Properties using AI dispatch report 25 to 35 percent faster average resolution times overall. The speed gain comes from instant vendor selection, parallel outreach to multiple vendors, and automated scheduling, all of which eliminate the sequential phone calls and waiting that slow down manual processes. What happens if the vendor doesn’t respond to the AI’s message? AI vendor communication systems include built-in escalation logic. If a vendor doesn’t acknowledge the dispatch within a configured timeframe, the AI automatically contacts backup vendors, alerts the property manager, or both. This is one of the strongest arguments for AI: it never forgets to follow up. VendorAccess.com recommends vendors respond to new work orders within 1 business hour on weekdays. AI can enforce that standard consistently. Does AI vendor communication work after hours? Yes, and after hours is arguably when it provides the most value. Maintenance emergencies don’t wait for business hours, and most property management teams aren’t staffed to handle overnight vendor coordination. AI operates 24/7, triaging incoming requests, dispatching vendors for true emergencies, and queuing non-urgent issues for the next business day. What PMS systems does AI vendor communication integrate with? This varies by provider. The best systems integrate with major platforms like AppFolio, Buildium, Yardi, and others through API connections that allow the AI to create work orders, update statuses, and log notes directly within the PMS. Always verify integration depth before committing to a platform. How does AI vendor communication affect vendor relationships? When done well, it improves them. Vendors receive clearer job descriptions, complete context upfront, and consistent follow-up. They waste fewer trips on poorly scoped assignments and experience less of the communication chaos that leads to frustration. NARPM’s data showing 4.3 lost vendor relationships per year due to communication breakdowns suggests there’s significant room for improvement over the manual status quo. Is AI vendor communication the same as vendor dispatch software? No. Vendor dispatch software focuses on assigning work orders. AI vendor communication manages the entire maintenance communication lifecycle, including scheduling, follow-up, escalation, and documentation. Can AI communicate with multiple vendors simultaneously? Yes. AI can contact multiple vendors at the same time, compare response rates, and select the first qualified contractor to accept the assignment. Is AI vendor communication suitable for small property management companies? Yes. Smaller portfolios often experience the greatest administrative burden because maintenance coordination responsibilities are concentrated among fewer employees. Can vendors opt out of AI communication? Most systems allow vendors to choose their preferred communication channels, including SMS, email, and voice.

title: How Lam's Global Lab Network Compresses the Path From Discovery to Fab Deployment
summary: Lam's labs are part of a purpose-built, globally integrated R&D infrastructure designed to accelerate innovation across technology inflections.
body_text: Blog How Lam's Global Lab Network Compresses the Path From Discovery to Fab Deployment Wayne Nobles Aug 13, 2026 | Industry Technology Print Page Email URL RSS Feed Facebook Share Button Twitter Share Button Linkedin Share Button Lam’s global lab network connects semiconductor R&D, product development, customer collaboration, and digital modeling into a single innovation system The network supports innovation across AI, DRAM, NAND, logic, advanced packaging, and emerging semiconductor technologies Globally connected labs help accelerate experimentation, validation, and process development by sharing expertise and insights across regions, 24/7 Technology labs located near our customers have shrunk learning cycles from months to weeks and demonstrated process development timelines up to 2.5 times faster than previous approaches Lam intends to invest more than $3 billion in the next five years to expand its global R&D lab network, expecting to increase experimentation capacity by more than 50% Each new generation of semiconductor devices brings greater complexity, tighter process requirements, and increasing pressure to move faster from discovery to production. Today, AI is amplifying those demands. Advanced AI systems require higher-performance logic, sophisticated memory architectures, and increasingly complex packaging technologies. At the same time, the industry continues to push forward in NAND, DRAM , logic scaling , and advanced packaging. Long before the current AI boom, Lam recognized that semiconductor progress would increasingly depend on the velocity with which engineers, customers, tools, expertise, and data could come together to solve complex challenges. The result is a purpose-built, globally integrated R&D infrastructure designed to accelerate innovation across technology inflections. With the pace of AI accelerating, our investment years ago has become a decisive advantage in this AI era. What Is Lam's Global Lab Network? Lam’s global lab network is an integrated R&D system of specialized labs worldwide, each purpose-built to accelerate a distinct step of the semiconductor innovation cycle — from foundational research and pathfinding to product development, customer qualification, and fab deployment. Together, these labs connect tools, data, expertise, and customer collaboration across locations and time zones so innovation can move in parallel and at scale. Lam’s global lab network spans the U.S., Asia, and Europe. The combined R&D infrastructure supports more than one million experiments annually. Facilities specialized for foundational research in new chemistries, materials, and mechatronics can compress weeks of experimental work into as little as days. Process development labs carry those advances toward production readiness, with engineering, product development, and manufacturing teams working side by side on the same tools. Located in proximity to customers, Lam’s technology centers support rapid qualification and validation alongside customers' engineering teams. These facilities operate as a connected innovation system, 24 hours a day, seven days a week, enabling innovation in parallel and at scale. The strategy means faster research, experimentation, testing, and deployment of breakthrough semiconductor technology. Semiconductor Innovation Depends on Faster Learning As semiconductor devices become more advanced, velocity becomes a competitive advantage. Modern chips can feature structures only a few atoms wide and require hundreds of precisely controlled manufacturing steps. A change in one process can affect many others, making development increasingly complex and interconnected. Success depends on identifying viable solutions earlier, validating them faster, and sharing knowledge more effectively across teams. That’s why Lam’s strategy focuses on accelerating learning cycles (not simply increasing laboratory capacity). The company’s global lab network brings together specialized expertise, advanced tools, and collaborative infrastructure designed to help engineers move more quickly from experimentation to outcomes for our customers. Why a Globally Connected Lab Network Matters Because the network connects tools, data, and expertise across locations and time zones, work does not have to move in a single linear sequence. Insights from one lab can inform work elsewhere in the network, helping teams make progress in parallel, reduce idle time between development steps, and compress the path from pathfinding to fab deployment. The result is an operating system for innovation and velocity, strategically designed to accelerate process development across increasingly complex semiconductor technologies. Proven Results: Faster Process Development Across Lam’s global R&D infrastructure, the network supports more than one million experiments annually, a scale of learning that matters as device architectures become more complex and development windows compress. In our foundational research facilities, Lam has already shown how bringing early materials and process screening in-house can compress learning cycles. Work that once relied on outside labs and could take months can now deliver first-wafer results in weeks, helping teams learn faster, understand why paths fail, and move promising technologies forward with greater confidence. Recent engagements in labs close to customers have shrunk learning cycles from months to weeks and demonstrated process development timelines up to 2.5 times faster than previous approaches. These examples demonstrate how proximity, specialization, and global connectivity can combine to accelerate semiconductor innovation. More than $3 Billion Investment in Future Semiconductor Innovation Lam is expanding this proven model with intends to invest more than $3 billion in the next five years to grow its global R&D lab network. The planned multi-site expansion is expected to add infrastructure and capabilities to increase experiment capacity by more than 50%, helping further compress the path from early research and pathfinding to product development, customer qualification, and fab deployment. This is not a response to a single market trend. It is an expansion of a long-term strategy built around increasing innovation velocity across multiple technology cycles. As device architectures become more complex and development requirements continue to grow, investments in infrastructure, expertise, and collaborative R&D capabilities become increasingly important. Built for Whatever Comes Next The semiconductor roadmap is not slowing down. New architectures, materials, and process requirements have continued to raise the bar for precision and speed. Lam’s global lab network was built for that reality: specialized where deep expertise matters, close to customers where collaboration matters, and integrated globally so learning can move faster than any single lab could move alone. Lam’s global lab network was built to anticipate that reality. It brings together specialized facilities, customer collaboration, and global expertise into a single system designed to accelerate innovation throughout the semiconductor development lifecycle. Wayne Nobles is corporate vice president, Global Products Operation Frequently Asked Questions What is Lam’s global lab network? Lam’s global lab network is a connected system of semiconductor R&D facilities that supports foundational research, technology pathfinding, product development, customer collaboration, process testing, qualification, and deployment. Specialized centers are integrated through shared expertise, data, tools, and digital capabilities, operating 24/7, enabling innovation in parallel and at scale. How does Lam accelerate semiconductor process development? Lam combines specialized research labs, product development centers, customer technology centers, digital tools, and global collaboration to shorten learning cycles. This approach helps engineers test ideas, share insights, identify viable solutions, and move technologies toward production more efficiently. Recent customer engagements in our technology center has enabled Lam to shorten process development up to 2.5 times. Why is semiconductor innovation becoming more complex? AI, advanced memory architectures, shrinking device dimensions, new materials, and increasingly sophisticated packaging are creating more complex process and integration requirements. Chip fabrication can involve hundreds of tightly connected steps, making early learning and precise process control increasingly important. How does Lam’s lab network support AI chip development? The network supports process and equipment innovation for technologies that enable AI computing, including advanced logic, high-performance memory, NAND, and advanced packaging. Its integrated model helps accelerate experimentation, validation, qualification, and the transition to high-volume manufacturing. How much is Lam investing in its global lab network? Lam intends to invest more than $3 billion over five years to expand its global lab network. The investment is expected to add infrastructure and capabilities to increase experimentation capacity by more than 50%. Which semiconductor technologies can benefit from Lam’s lab network? The network supports innovation across logic, DRAM, NAND, AI chips, advanced packaging, panel-level processing, and emerging device architectures. Its integrated development model is designed to adapt as new semiconductor technology inflections emerge. Why are global semiconductor research labs important? Globally connected semiconductor research labs allow companies to combine specialized expertise, customer proximity, physical tools, data, and digital tools across regions, 24/7. This can improve experimentation efficiency, accelerate learning, and shorten the path from early research to manufacturable solutions. title: Introduction to renewable natural gas
summary: What is renewable natural gas? Renewable natural gas (RNG) differs from fossil fuels as it's produced from various types of waste, like used cooking oil, animal waste, sludge from wastewater, manure and other waste materials. As these biodegradable materials decompose, methane is released. This methane is captured and converted into RNG.
body_text: Introduction to renewable natural gas Originally published January 2024; Updated August 2026 By Imon Uduehi, General Manager - Alternate Fuels and Fuel Delivery Systems Aug 10, 2026 What is renewable natural gas? Renewable natural gas (RNG) differs from fossil fuels as it's produced from various types of waste, like used cooking oil, animal waste, sludge from wastewater, manure and other waste materials. As these biodegradable materials decompose, methane is released. This methane is captured and converted into RNG. Because methane is the primary component of natural gas, RNG is interchangeable with natural gas derived from fossil fuels. In other words, RNG can be used in natural gas engines without any modifications. When you hear the term RNG, envision it as a renewable and clean energy source that contributes to decarbonizing the world, rather than as a fossil fuel. This is why Cummins is excited about RNG and its potential applications in the trucking industry. Is renewable natural gas carbon-negative? A carbon negative index, also known as a carbon index, is a measure used to assess the environmental impact of various fuels. If a fuel contributes to lowering the amount of carbon dioxide (CO2) in the atmosphere, it is considered carbon-negative. The carbon intensity of RNG depends on the type of feedstock used to produce it. For instance, when RNG is derived from sources like manure, chicken waste or dairy waste the carbon intensity is extremely low and therefore the negative index can be substantially higher. When RNG is produced from food waste or landfills, it is still negative but has a slightly higher carbon intensity than animal waste. RNG is not merely an environmentally friendly alternative to conventional natural gas and other fossil fuels, but is also a proactive solution to reducing CO2 emissions and combating climate change. Broader adoption of RNG in natural gas engines could lead to a significant reduction in CO2 emissions. This is a key reason why 98 percent of all natural gas vehicles in California and approximately 64 percent of natural gas vehicles in the United States run on RNG. Additionally, feedstocks used to produce RNG, if left to decay naturally, produce methane gas emissions, a greenhouse gas that is 25 times more potent than CO2. By capturing and using this waste to produce RNG, these potential greenhouse gas emissions are prevented. RNG engine considerations Cummins natural gas engines can run on RNG with no modifications, offering similar performance to diesel engines but with quieter operations and environmental benefits. In 2024, Cummins will launch the latest natural gas engine, the X15N. The X15N is an EPA and CARB-compliant engine with power ratings up to 500 HP and torque up to 1850 lb-ft. It’s an ideal heavy-duty engine for many long-haul applications . Interested in learning more about energy transition basics?
